newsitem.title: USA: Senate votes expanded probe of fundraising.
newsitem.headline: Senate votes expanded probe of fundraising.

text.p: The Senate voted on Tuesday for a sweeping investigation into campaign fund-raising abuses after Republican leaders backed down from demands for a limited probe of only illegal activities.

After lengthy negotiations among Republicans who control the Senate and minority Democrats, the Senate agreed to a deal to expand the probe from only illegal fund raising to both "illegal and improper" activities.

The plan to expand the probe came on a unanimous 99 to 0 vote on an amendment to a measure that would authorise spending $4.35 million to look into fund-raising irregularities, with the focus on foreign donations to Democrats for President Bill Clinton's 1996 campaign.
The vote effectively ended weeks of a stalemate and arguments between Republicans and Democrats over the scope of the investigation by the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee.

An expanded investigation was exactly what Democrats wanted over objections of Republicans who did not want the Governmental Affairs Committee to delve into possibly embarrassing activities involving congressional races.

Earlier in the day, Senate Republicans agreed to a deal and gave in to Democratic demands for a wider probe once Republicans realised they faced an apparent defeat of a plan to just look at "illegal" activities.

By expanding the scope to "improper" as well as illegal, the Senate investigators can look into perfectly legal but questionable unregulated "soft money" donations -- many affecting Republican campaigns as well as Democratic ones.

While donors to individual federal candidates are limited to giving $1,000, donations of any size can go to political parties for party building, get-out-the-vote campaigns and other activities. Republicans traditionally outraise Democrats in this area, which is called soft money.
